independentReview.reviewerNote: Independent exact-head review by chatgpt-hq, which authored no commit in the proof delta. The reviewer's verdict was that #399's actual defect is repaired: both extraction readers call the same joinScopeBullet rule, the continuation opt-in is confined to the claim `Write scope` field, table rows remain one-line, unwrapped bullets preserve their old trim semantics, and the shared case matrix plus the pre-fix sensitivity control is appropriate regression evidence.

acceptanceNote: #399's acceptance is met at this head and is checkable from strings alone. (1) `parseClaim` and `scopeTextFromBody` use ONE shared continuation rule -- `joinScopeBullet` in scripts/lib/claim-scope.mjs -- so a wrapped `- Write scope:` bullet can no longer silently declare only a prefix. (2) A shared case list, tools/entry/scope-continuation.test.mjs, is exercised through BOTH readers: 13 cases covering wrapped and one-line-equivalent scopes, termination at the next `-` bullet, `*` bullet, blank line, heading and table row, both bold label spellings, end-of-body, and CRLF in both shapes. (3) A sensitivity control, `preFixOneLineRead`, reproduces the pre-#399 one-line reader and is asserted WRONG on every wrapped case and RIGHT on every unwrapped one, with a further assertion that the old read yields a strict PREFIX rather than an error -- so the guard can fail. Falsifiability verified by mutation, not by reading: temporarily flipping `continued: true` to `false` fails 23 assertions. (4) Behaviour outside the contract is preserved and pinned: `- scope:` stays a claim-only alias, table rows stay one line, every other parseClaim/parseHandoff field stays one line, and missing or empty bullets stay null in both readers.
scopeHonestyNote: What #407 proves is narrower than "one continuation parser everywhere", and this receipt states the limit rather than letting a later reader over-read it. Only the TWO scope-bullet extraction readers implicated by #399 now share `joinScopeBullet`. `parseWriteScope` in scripts/lib/claim-scope.mjs still contains a third, raw-markdown bullet-boundary rule; it is unreachable through the two repaired paths because both feed it already-extracted one-line scope text, which is why it does not block this closure. Separately, `ENDS_SCOPE_BULLET` does not terminate on numbered-list items or fenced code blocks. Both are the reviewer's non-blocking findings, both are queued for the parser-consolidation lane, and neither is repaired here because a repair would invalidate review 5151177996.
